subject: SLOs + reproducibility checklist — Horizon discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nakhil@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@horizonai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: SLOs + reproducibility checklist — Horizon discovery follow-up

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth we can iterate on: 

Summary of requirements we captured
- Latency (sync): p95 <= 200 ms for typical prompt (avg ~120 tokens).
- Streaming: per-token emission latency <= 30 ms p95, support chunked streaming with server-side keepalive.
- Throughput: sustained 400 RPS for steady-state, burstable to 800 RPS for short windows.
- Concurrency: support 60 concurrent sessions with KV cache per session (cache size ~50k tokens).
- Input sizes: typical request ~120 tokens, occasional up to 1,024 tokens.
- Reproducibility: need a repeatable harness (seeded pseudo-randomness), measurement rules, and request sampling rules tied to production traces.

What I attached / links
- prompt_sets_v1.jsonl — example prompt bundle (small dev set + representative production-sampled prompts).
- eval_harness_config.yaml — initial harness configuration (measurement windows, warmup, client headers to tag requests).
- Drive folder with extended artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-horizon-perf

Proposed immediate next steps (please confirm):
1) You confirm average request size and max length acceptance (we used avg 120 / max 1024 above).
2) We run a small reproducibility pass (30-minute run) using the attached prompt set and provide raw logs + load generator config.
3) Post-run: joint readout to review p50/p95/p99 latencies, tail behavior, and streaming token emission times.

If that looks right, we’ll prioritize a short-run in the next 48–72 hours (we can do an overnight window to match your traffic profile if you prefer).

Thanks — I’ll loop Soojin in for the harness run.

— Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLOs + reproducibility checklist — Horizon discovery follow-up

Thanks, Nikhil — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we commit to a run: 

1) Streaming semantics: when you say "per-token emission <= 30 ms p95" are you measuring from token-generation completion on the server to network write, or end-to-end client receive time (i.e., includes network RTT)? We need end-to-end numbers if possible.

2) Cache behavior: our sessions rely on a fairly large KV cache for personalization. The 50k-token cache you mentioned — do you have recommendations for eviction policy and warm-up steps for the harness?

3) Workload sampling: we can export production traces, but they contain PII. What's the best pattern for us to provide representative traces safely (anonymized, tokenized)?

4) Measurement window: for initial reproducibility proof, would a 30-minute run with 10 minutes warmup + 20 minutes measurement be sufficient? We prefer multi-hour runs for final numbers but understand early passes can be shorter.

Also legal asked whether Redwood can provide a short SOC2 artifacts checklist ahead of a larger PoC. Procurement cc'd here (procurement@horizonai.com).

If you confirm point (1) and (3) we’ll pull an anonymized trace extract and get it to you.

— Sam
Director, Platform Engineering | Horizon AI
sam.green@horizonai.com

Adding operational detail for the proposed run plan so we can move quickly once Sam confirms: 

Run plan (internal)
- Run types: 1) synthetic (no PII) using tokenized trace surrogates, 2) production-sampled (anonymized) once legal signs off.
- Warmup: 10 minutes / 100k tokens (whichever comes first) to populate KV caches.
- Measurement: 20 minutes steady-state window for initial pass (report p50/p95/p99, streaming per-token jitter).
- Randomization: harness will use a fixed RNG seed for the first reproducibility pass; we'll snapshot the seed and request ids.
- Instrumentation: include client headers x-hz-request-id and x-hz-session-id; server will log per-token timestamps.
- Variability tests: run 3 replicates separated by jittered start times to observe run-to-run variance.

Action items for us
- Soojin: generate a mini-harness runbook (markdown) with concrete commands and the exact k6/locust profiles. Attach here as mini-harness-runbook.md.
- Nikhil: coordinate with Sam on anonymized trace export and preferred test windows.

If legal needs a SOC2 checklist, I can share the standard artifacts we hand to SOC2 reviewers — copying a short checklist below for now so procurement has visibility:
- System architecture diagram (obfuscate customer-specific segments)
- Data flow & retention policy summary
- Access control matrix and recent audit log samples (redacted)

— Ben
Staff Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLOs + reproducibility checklist — Horizon discovery follow-up

Hi Sam — thanks for the quick turn. I can own the mini-run. Quick answers and a proposed timeline: 

Answers
1) Measurement framing: for the initial pass we'll report both server-side emission latency and end-to-end client-observed latency (we'll run the client and server in the same region to keep network RTT minimal, and report both numbers so you can add your network delta).
2) Cache policy: we recommend LRU with a per-session soft limit of 50k tokens and eviction logging enabled. For harness warmup we’ll replay the top-20 heavy sessions from your anonymized sample to prime personalization caches.
3) Traces: please provide a tokenized, anonymized export (no raw PII fields). If you prefer, we can provide a small script that tokenizes and replaces identifiers with stable pseudonyms before upload.
4) Measurement window: 10 minute warmup + 20 minute measurement for the first pass is fine — we'll run three replicates across different start times and share the raw CSVs.

Proposed timeline
- Monday (May 24): we ship harness commands + k6 profiles and final prompt_set with fixed seeds.
- Tuesday (May 25) overnight: short-run (30 minutes) then same-day readout.

Ask of you: can you confirm the acceptable test window (UTC offsets) and sign off on the prompt set in the Drive link? Also legal/procurement — if you can share the minimal SOC2 checklist contact, Ben will provide the redacted artifacts.

I’ll attach the runbook and follow-up with exact commands.

— Soojin Lee
Performance Lead | Redwood Inference
